did_you_know.text: The chapter opens during the wheat harvest. Samson went to visit his wife, carrying a young goat, but her father would not let him enter her room.
Samson’s wife’s father claimed that he thought Samson hated her, so he had given her to Samson’s companion. He offered Samson her younger sister instead.
Samson caught three hundred foxes, tied them together in pairs by their tails, and fastened a torch between each pair of tails.
After setting the torches alight, Samson released the foxes into the fields of the Philistines. The fire burned the standing grain, the stacks of grain, and the olive orchards.
The Philistines discovered that Samson was responsible for burning the fields because his wife had been given to his companion. In retaliation, they burned the woman and her father.
Samson struck the Philistines with a great blow, described as “thigh and hip,” and then went to live in the cleft of the rock of Etam.
The Philistines camped in Judah, and the men of Judah explained that they had come to capture Samson and hand him over to the Philistines because the Philistines ruled over them.

Three thousand men from Judah went down to the rock of Etam. In their words to Samson, they expressed their fear of Philistine rule and their opposition to his actions, which had brought conflict upon them.
When Samson reached Lehi, the Spirit of the Lord came powerfully upon him. The ropes on his arms melted like flax burned in the fire, and he broke free.
Samson found a fresh donkey’s jawbone and struck down a thousand men with it. Afterward, the place was called Ramath-lehi.
After his victory, Samson became very thirsty and called out to the Lord. He acknowledged that God had given him this great deliverance and asked not to die of thirst.
God split open the hollow place at Lehi, and water came out. Samson drank, his spirit returned, and he recovered; so the place was called En Hakkore.
The chapter concludes by stating that Samson judged Israel for twenty years, during the period when the Philistines ruled over Israel.
